chunks: It is narrated from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one who narrated to him, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked about the time of Maghrib.
He said: 'When its pedestal disappears.' I said: 'And what is its pedestal?' He said: 'Its disk.' I said: 'When does its disk disappear?' He said: 'When you look at it and do not see it.'

key_terms.قُرْصُهَا: Its disk (referring to the visible body of the sun)
key_terms.كُرْسِيُّهَا: Its pedestal (referring to the sun's position or base)
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: The time of Maghrib (the afternoon prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the precise definition of the Maghrib prayer time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment for Maghrib prayer by distinguishing between the sun's disk (qursh) and its 'pedestal' (kursiyy), a terminology rooted in classical Arabic astronomical descriptions. The Imam establishes the practical criterion as the moment the sun's disk visually vanishes from the horizon, marking the onset of twilight (shafaq) and the end of the sunset phase. This definition aligns with the majority of Shia jurists who prioritize the disappearance of the sun's disk over other indicators for the start of Maghrib time.
